title: Sodium Correction: Avoiding Overly Rapid Changes
subject: Electrolytes
preview: Serum sodium reflects water balance relative to solute, so the cause of dysnatremia matters as much as the number.
quickRevision: Serum sodium reflects water balance relative to solute, so the cause of dysnatremia matters as much as the number.
Assess symptoms, serum osmolality, volume status and medications before selecting correction strategies.
Severe neurologic symptoms require urgent supervised treatment and repeated sodium measurements.

sections.title: Interpret the result in context
points: Serum sodium reflects water balance relative to solute, so the cause of dysnatremia matters as much as the number.
Rapid correction of chronic hyponatremia risks osmotic demyelination, especially in vulnerable patients.

sections.title: Clinical interpretation & next steps
points: Assess symptoms, serum osmolality, volume status and medications before selecting correction strategies.
Severe neurologic symptoms require urgent supervised treatment and repeated sodium measurements.

sections.title: Exam trap — avoid this mistake
points: Do not apply a single unmonitored correction plan to every patient, particularly when chronicity is uncertain.

quiz.question: What is a feared complication of overly rapid correction of chronic hyponatremia?
quiz.explanation: Rapid correction of chronic hyponatremia risks osmotic demyelination, especially in vulnerable patients.
